title: fix: reduce cloud snapshot setup latency
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Snapshot-backed cloud sessions wait for redundant remote commands, and a busy Gateway startup can replace a healthy configured Crabbox CLI with an older managed fallback.

## User Impact

Project preparation and initial snapshot capture each save a remote command round trip. This improves cold preparation and changed-commit starts; same-commit reuse keeps its existing verification path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Seed installation completes the prepared checkout in the same command when the admitted project has no executable setup recipe or setup was explicitly skipped. Executable recipes keep their separate authority check before execution.

Runtime preparation and credential scrubbing also share one command. The shell clears forwarded credentials before scrubbing, and native capture still waits for successful cleanup and a current owner. A cleanup failure now stops the incomplete project worker and reports the error before enrollment. Teardown captures retain their existing warning and cleanup behavior.

The configured CLI version probe now allows 30 seconds. A live startup trace showed the healthy probe finishing after 6.9 seconds, beyond the previous five-second budget, and triggering an unnecessary managed fallback. The fake-clock regression verifies that a seven-second successful probe keeps the configured CLI without downloading or writing managed state.

CI also exposed brittle Signal-test synchronization. The test-only fix observes an actual pending retry and verifies Stop cancels it without another dispatch; the adjacent drain check controls an in-flight send and keeps assertions outside the stream reconnect callback.

## Evidence

- 219 focused tests passed across project preparation, Crabbox provisioning, image reuse, retirement, recovery, and managed CLI selection. The new regressions fail against the original code for the expected extra command round trips and replacement of the configured CLI with the older managed version.
- Focused test runs with one worker: core files 160.59 seconds wall; Crabbox files 166.25 seconds wall, including compiler/cache setup. The final moved-test/managed-CLI run passed 38 tests in 80.87 seconds wall. New recipe cases took 2.5–5.2 seconds each under varying host load; the fake-clock version regression took 6 milliseconds; the real shell fixture verifies credential removal, retained archive bytes, and capture ordering without network access or package installation.
- Changed-file repository checks passed, including core/plugin type checks, lint, boundaries, assertion safety, and formatting. Independent Codex review found no actionable findings through P2.
- Live AWS/Linux proof at head `e681148f6d4f34cc5bfb18669dd1e29de2fb1cd0`: the combined runtime-and-scrub command returned exit 0 at 21:22:18.697 UTC; native checkpoint creation began at 21:22:18.809 UTC and succeeded. Enrollment began afterward. A second session forked that same checkpoint, reached active placement with a newly enrolled node, and passed exact Git HEAD and fixture-content checks on its recorded lease/workspace. Read-only inspection of the surviving fork also confirmed the original source-lease state was absent, fresh fork enrollment state was present, and there were zero captured runtime-preparation scripts, scrub scripts, or forwarded-environment artifacts. Fresh-fork/proof scripts were distinguished from captured source artifacts. The independent generated-shell regression verifies cleanup, credential isolation, and retained archive bytes at the capture boundary.
- The original startup path was also exercised live: a healthy CLI probe took 6.922 seconds with the old code and selected managed 0.56; the candidate took 6.803 seconds and retained configured 0.64 without fallback or cloud allocation.
- The synthetic two-file project's Git preparation changed from four remote commands (72.8 and 76.1 seconds in baseline samples) to three (69.0 seconds in the candidate). Runtime preparation and scrubbing also changed from two commands to one. End-to-end cold times were 395.3 seconds baseline and 495.3 seconds candidate because provider warmup and runtime download/install varied substantially. Same-commit reuse was 168.8 seconds baseline and 131.2 seconds candidate; that code path is unchanged, so this difference is not attributed to the patch.
- Changed-commit preparation improved from four commands / 93.6 seconds to three / 74.6 seconds (19.0 seconds, about 20%). End-to-end dispatch was 220.4 seconds baseline and 222.9 seconds candidate: the candidate native fork took 18 seconds longer and masked the preparation saving. Exact Git HEAD and file checks passed; the foreground session retained the original image. A provider HTTP 500 had interrupted an earlier allocation before remote preparation; that lease was stopped and this measurement used a fresh allocation. The exact prepared reserve was then consumed in 3.447 seconds, or 6.418 seconds including session creation; its Git HEAD and file checks passed. Background preparation took 278.4 seconds and published the refreshed commit image. Refill was disabled before cleanup.
- CI found existing Workshop and compaction fixture failures, repaired on main in [764c9331a31b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/764c9331a31b4b87bdc06b95f39c6870c5aca2f3) and [c947420a3236](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c947420a323614f7b0d637652d238f2c5db965bd). The Signal fixture repair is included here. Snapshot production code remains byte-identical to the live-tested `e681148f` implementation.
- Signal validation used the actual failing CI merge and original 51-file plan: 977 tests passed in 106.28 seconds. Final focused validation passed 6 tests in 55.69 seconds including cold transforms; changed cases took 1.381 / 1.609 seconds. A missing-retry-abort-binding negative control failed at the intended precondition. The historical five-second timeout did not reproduce locally; local macOS/Node 24.21 differs from CI Linux/Node 24.19, and a short temporary path avoided unrelated macOS Unix-socket limits. Typed lint and extension-test type checks passed.
- All owned AWS leases and checkpoints, test Gateways, and callback tunnels were authoritatively verified cleaned up. The interrupted provider attempt and its cleanup reconciliation remain recorded separately from the successful continuation.
